items.text: Opportunity cost is the value of what you give up by choosing one path over the other.
This does not apply to very cheap online courses.
For skills like coding, digital marketing, data analysis, design, or sales, the market rewards a portfolio and results more than a certificate.

If you move to a paid course, judge that specific course, not its platform: check the instructor's track record, how recently it was updated, whether it includes real projects and feedback, refund terms, and independent reviews from actual learners, not star ratings alone.

blocks.heading: Hybrid Path: Work First, Study Later

items.text: For graduates who are neither funded nor certain, "work first, then study" is usually the strongest option on the table, not a compromise, a genuinely different and often better-sequenced plan.
Take a job in or close to your target field, even if it is not the dream role.
Prioritise a role that teaches something transferable over one that pays slightly more but teaches nothing.

items.text: Research or academic paths, where a continuous line from bachelor's to master's to a research track (or PhD later) is the normal, expected route.
Specialized engineering or science roles where the entry-level job itself requires an M.Tech or MS, so delaying study just delays entry into the field entirely.
You have secured funding, a scholarship, family support without strain, or an assistantship, removing the debt-and-repayment risk from the decision.
You can name the exact target role and specialization the degree leads to, and have verified real job postings asking for that exact combination.
